memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'If a descendant of Aaron has a defiling skin disease or a bodily
discharge, he may not eat the sacred offerings until he is cleansed.
He will also be unclean if he touches something defiled by a corpse or
by anyone who has an emission of semen, or if he touches any crawling
thing that makes him unclean, or any person who makes him unclean,
whatever the uncleanness may be'" - Lev 22:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a very earthy list. Skin disease, bodily discharges, contact
with a dead body, touching a crawling creature. These were not moral
sins. Most were simply the ordinary realities of living in a human
body in a fallen world.

That tells us something worth noticing. God's law reached into the
plainest, least glamorous corners of daily life. Nothing was too
mundane for Him to address. He was teaching Israel, through their
bodies and their routines, that sin had touched everything - even the
things nobody chose.

Dear friend, we sometimes imagine God is interested only in the
spiritual parts of our lives: our prayers, our church attendance, our
big decisions. Leviticus says otherwise. The God of Scripture cares
about the kitchen, the sickbed, the workplace, the body you live in.

Paul captures it beautifully: whether you eat or drink or whatever you
do, do it all for the glory of God (1 Cor 10:31). And he urges us to
offer our bodies as living sacrifices - our actual physical lives - as
true worship (Rom 12:1).

Your ordinary Tuesday is not outside God's interest. He is Lord of all
of it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which parts of my life do I treat as "not spiritual enough" for God?
2. How could I offer my ordinary work to God as worship this week?
3. Does my faith reach into my body, my health, my habits?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You are Lord of my whole life, not just the religious parts.
Take my ordinary hours and let them be worship offered to You. Amen.
